subject: AI & Agents
title: The Transformer Architecture
description: Learn The Transformer Architecture in one minute.

hook.text: Every major LLM — GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama — is built on the same 2017 invention.

buildup.text: The transformer uses self-attention to let every word look at every other word simultaneously.

discovery.text: Unlike older models that read left-to-right, transformers process entire sequences at once.

twist.text: This parallelism is why transformers train so efficiently on GPUs.

climax.text: The architecture is surprisingly simple — attention layers stacked with feed-forward networks.

punchline.text: Simple parts, stacked deep, produce something extraordinary.

quiz.question: What is the key advantage of the transformer architecture?
options: It processes all words in a sequence simultaneously
It reads text one character at a time

details.summary: The Transformer is the neural network architecture behind all modern LLMs. Introduced in the 2017 'Attention Is All You Need' paper, it replaced older approaches with a parallel, attention-based design that scales efficiently.
details.whyItMatters: Transformers enabled the GPT, BERT, and LLaMA breakthroughs. Understanding this architecture is key to grasping how modern AI processes language and why recent progress has been so rapid.
takeaways: Transformers use self-attention to process all words simultaneously
They replaced sequential RNNs with parallel, scalable computation
Every major LLM — GPT, BERT, LLaMA — is built on Transformers

faq.question: Why did Transformers replace previous architectures?
faq.answer: Earlier RNNs processed words one at a time, creating bottlenecks with long sequences. Transformers process all words in parallel using attention, enabling faster training on GPUs and better handling of long-range dependencies.

faq.question: What are the main components of a Transformer?
faq.answer: Self-attention layers that let each word attend to every other, feed-forward networks for processing, positional encodings for word order, and layer normalization for training stability. These components stack into deep networks.
